title: The Compass and the South Gate
story:
High above Oakhaven, the wind off Cloudveil Ridge smelled of damp stone and pine needles. He had walked past the quiet stalls of Weaver's Wharf. He had listened to the steady hum of Mateo's loom. He had played among the wild ferns of the Terrace Gardens. Now, standing beside Barnaby on the high stone balcony, James looked at the fresh charcoal mark on his parchment map and knew that his time in the Grand Library was coming to an end. The town below was no longer a confusing maze of chimneys and cobblestones; it was a place with names, faces, and stories he carried with him.

Barnaby smiled softly, his hand resting on the balcony railing. From his pocket, the old clockmaker produced a small, polished brass pocket compass suspended from a thin cord. "If you're heading toward the ridge," Barnaby said gently, "the roads tend to twist beneath the canopy of pines. This will help you keep your true south." James accepted the compass carefully, feeling its tiny needle tremble and align itself with the distant peaks. He tucked it safely inside his brass canister alongside his map, securing the lid tight.

After returning to his cozy Archive Nook one last time to collect his remaining treasures, James descended the spiral stairs and walked through the grand south portal of the library. He stepped onto South Gate Avenue, a wide cobblestone thoroughfare lined with tall pine trees and fragrant woodsmoke. The roar of the city's central market faded behind him, replaced by the deep, rhythmic creaking of timber wagons preparing for the mountain pass.

James paused at the edge of the avenue, resting a hand on his colorful woven strap. High above, the library's copper dome glinted in the afternoon sun, a beacon resting on its hill. He looked down the long road stretching toward the misty foothills of Cloudveil Ridge, watching the tiny shadows of pines lengthen across the stone. He did not know what lay beyond the southern gates, but as he felt the cool mountain wind lift his fur, he knew he was ready to find out.
